verdicts.corrected_location: src/components/work/detail/work-deliverable-stage.tsx:33-44,74-77 (stale fallback promise in its header comment at 25-29)
verdicts.reasoning: READ: stagedArtifact keeps only canPreviewArtifact kinds (stage:34), and canPreviewArtifact is site|report|spreadsheet (work-site-preview.tsx:164-166). The stage is mounted only in TerminalRun (work-run-panel.tsx:356-358). rg for WorkDocuments/DocumentCard finds only the definition (work-documents.tsx:111,243) and no importer. SessionOutputs builds tiles from chat `artifacts` only (session-outputs.tsx:97-106) and has no Work reference at all. /artifacts and /library have no WorkArtifact reads either: rg for workArtifact.findMany in src finds only the API route and sync-entities. The runner does not post a chat message with links (no message.create in work-runner.ts). Run notifications carry no download links (rg in src/lib/work/notify). The stage's own comment (25-29) says Office kinds 'have a card in the rail's Outputs section', and that rail no longer exists. Correction: PDF is not in the runner's generated kinds. The deliverable spec union is document/spreadsheet/presentation/report/site (deliverables/index.ts:107-113), so the affected kinds are .docx and .pptx. .xlsx is staged. Merge impact: this is the core gap a unified artifact surface must close.

READ: the purge collects only prisma.attachment storageKeys plus thumbnails and the avatar (41-53), then prisma.user.delete runs (72). WorkArtifact cascades from User (schema.prisma:2630) and WorkArtifactVersion cascades from WorkArtifact (2660), so the rows vanish. Runner objects live at `work-artifacts/<userId>/...` (work-runner.ts:1988) and cloud files at `work/<userId>/<sessionId>/<name>` (work-runner.ts:1474-1476). Route-written objects use buildObjectKey, which gives `uploads/<userId>/...` (storage.ts:49-51). rg for deleteObject call sites shows none that touch these keys, and no prefix-delete or ListObjects helper exists outside backup/restore scripts. This is a GDPR erasure failure, so the severity is justified.

READ: the UNSAFE_MARKUP regexes are tested against the full page text, including escaped prose. escapeHtml does not touch letters, '=', ':', '(' or '@'. VERIFIED by my own scratch probe through generateDeliverable. Each of these paragraphs gave ok=false: 'Set the flag one = true…' (inline event handler), 'Read javascript: the good parts.' (javascript: URL), 'We fetch (and cache)…' (browser network call) and 'Use @import…' (CSS @import). A plain sentence gave ok=true. INFERRED: code blocks such as `button.onclick = f` or `fetch(url)` in any JS docs site trip the same rules. The runner then tells the model the validator could not re-open the file and to say so (work-runner.ts:2081-2083), and it stores validatedAt=null. The inline preview renders the site anyway, because previewDoc does not rescan (work-site-preview.tsx:254-276).

READ: useWorkArtifactList refetches only on [load, produced, enabled] (work-documents.tsx:100-103). produced = deriveArtifacts(events).length (use-conversation-work.ts:233,244), and deriveArtifacts is a Map keyed by artifact id, so artifact_updated replaces the entry (work-detail-panels.tsx:181-202). The session emits artifact_updated for a reused id (runner/agent-core/src/work/session.ts:580-588), and the runner reuses the id across versions (work-runner.ts:1996-2028). `enabled` stays true through the end of the run, and nothing calls reload. The stage previews version={artifact.currentVersion} (stage:68-73), while Download has no version param (stage:58; work-transport.tsx:1603-1606) and serves the current version. INFERRED: the mismatch lasts until the conversation is reopened or the run writes a different artifact.

READ: WorkDeliverableStage (stage:41-80) never reads validatedAt. ClientWorkArtifact carries it (serializers.ts:444,458). The download route signals an unvalidated file only through X-Juno-Validated/X-Juno-Validation-Warning headers (download/route.ts:155-156), which a plain <a href> never surfaces. The inline site preview has no validation handling (rg 'validat' in work-site-preview.tsx finds only comments). VerdictLine and the 'not confirmed to open' label live only in the unmounted DocumentCard (work-documents.tsx:279). This contradicts schema.prisma:2621-2623. It overlaps with ux-3.

READ: discovery calls fetchWorkSessions({conversationId, limit: 1}) and adopts only result[0] (use-conversation-work.ts:179-186). ChatView inserts one WorkRunPanel, while research also maps history into HistoricalResearchRunPanel (chat-view.tsx:2262-2266). The limitation is acknowledged at 63-70. It is worse than stated: /work/<sessionId> still resolves a task to its conversation (src/app/(app)/work/[[...segments]]/page.tsx:49-58), and notification emails and schedule rows link through that path (commit ff3963ec message). A link to the older task A therefore lands on a chat that draws the newer task B. No other web surface lists a session's artifacts (see defect 1).

READ: the runner parses {spec: request.spec} with no provenance (work-runner.ts:1826). The tool deps type has only identifier and spec (runner/agent-core/src/work/tools.ts:949-952), and the inputSchema declares only those two (1017-1030). generateDeliverable defaults provenance to [] (deliverables/index.ts:181), so buildReport's sourcesMarkdown returns [] (report.ts:337-340) and the stored provenance is []. Citations exist only as source_cited events (session.ts:591-594). Caveat, which lowers practical impact but not correctness: the model can still write its own 'Sources' blocks as text, so 'cannot see where any figure came from' holds only when it does not. What is guaranteed dead in production is the structured provenance and the automatic Sources section.

READ: the bounds allow 20x500-char bullets, 10x2000-char paragraphs and 20x10 tables (presentation.ts:30-39). Text goes into fixed BODY_HEIGHT boxes at 16pt with no fit/autoFit option (~178-192). addTable has no h cap and no autoPage (~194-206). The header claims closed layouts prevent 'text running off the slide' (14-18). VERIFIED with my own probe: a 20-row table slide writes 21 <a:tr h="0"> rows in a frame at y=1280160 EMU (1.4in), and validation.ok is true. The row-height overflow math is INFERRED but plausible. The 10x2000-char body obviously cannot fit a ~3.6in box at 16pt.

READ: the replay short-circuits only on an equal contentHash with the head version (route.ts:282-300). VERIFIED with my own probe: generating the same document, spreadsheet or presentation spec twice 1.1s apart gives different hashes, while report and site are stable. It is latent, because no client POSTs: web transport has no POST to this path, native uses GET only (NativeWorkClient.swift:433-474), and the runner writes directly via storeDeliverable. Low is right.

READ: the title is skipped when blocks[0] is an H1 (242-248), but the subtitle is pushed unconditionally before the blocks (249-253). VERIFIED with my own probe: the w:t order is ["Sub","Body H1","p"].

READ: paragraphs go through escapeMarkdownLineStart (172), but list items (175-177) and quotes (181) use inlineMarkdown only. VERIFIED with my own probe: the output is '- 3. Third step
- - dash lead
- # not a heading

> # quoted hash', while the paragraph '# para hash' is correctly escaped to '\# para hash'. Under CommonMark the list items become a nested list, a nested bullet and a heading, and the quote contains a heading.

READ: `z.object({ date: z.string().datetime() })` (spreadsheet.ts:66), while the tool guide says '{ date: "<ISO 8601>" }' (runner/agent-core/src/work/tools.ts:971). A bare date is valid ISO 8601. VERIFIED with my own probe: {date:'2026-03-04'} fails with 'Invalid ISO datetime'. The zod message is returned verbatim to the model (work-runner.ts:1827-1831), so one retry recovers it.
READ: currency is '"$"#,##0.00' (spreadsheet.ts:85). The column schema has no currency-code field (88-93), and the tool guide offers only 'currency' (tools.ts:971). A non-USD budget always shows $.

READ: cellText returns String(value) for numbers and never reads numFmt. VERIFIED with my own probe: currency 1234.5, percent 0.256 and integer 1234567 preview as "1234.5","0.256","1234567". Spreadsheets are the one Office kind that is staged inline in chat, so this is reachable today.

READ: WorkDeliverablePreview returns WorkReportPreview for report, and WorkSitePreview for every other previewable kind (work-site-preview.tsx:353-357). The file has no spreadsheet dialog; the function list shows only SpreadsheetPreviewBody, which is used inline (855). DocumentCard shows Preview whenever canPreviewArtifact (work-documents.tsx:284-293, 419-428), and that includes spreadsheet. It is latent, because DocumentCard is unmounted, but it is exactly the misrouting the guard comment (342-352) warns about. It would bite any merged surface that re-mounts the cards.

READ: putObject runs before the transaction, and the transaction throws DeliverableError for a soft-deleted identifier or a kind conflict (1996-2006) with no deleteObject. The HTTP route runs the same two checks BEFORE its putObject (route.ts:247-280), so only the runner orphans on these refusals. No sweeper exists: rg for sweep/orphan and for work-artifacts keys in scripts and src/lib finds no collector. Other upload routes clean up on failure (upload/route.ts:135, attachments/[id]/versions/route.ts:125).

READ: the route enforces the IDENTIFIER regex and max length (route.ts:56,72). The tool only trims (tools.ts:1039-1040), even though its description promises 'Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore' (1021). The runner uses the raw string in the unique key and the object key (work-runner.ts:1988,1997). One part of the claim is REFUTED: the error does not 'escape the tool'. WorkSession wraps tool.execute in try/catch and returns 'Tool crashed: <message>' with isError=true (runner/agent-core/src/work/session.ts:933-940), so the model does get a (poor) correctable message. What remains is parity drift plus odd S3 keys, and on S3 'Q3 report/v1..final' is just a literal nested key rather than a traversal.

READ: the runner's stored validation object has no `details` key, whereas the route's validationForStorage writes details (route.ts:89-104). Impact today is nil: no consumer reads validation.details (serializers.ts has no 'details'; native reads only validation.ok at NativeWorkClient.swift:1135-1136). This is a latent inconsistency that matters only for a future card, so low is right.

READ: DELIVERABLE_VALIDATOR is still 'juno.work.deliverables.validate.v1' (validate.ts:255), and its comment (247-254) says it exists so that tightening rules does not relabel old verdicts. `git log -S validate.v1` shows it introduced only in f66876db (2026-08-05). f490ff0e (2026-08-08, +146 lines in validate.ts) added packageBudgetProblems, relationship checks, formula and overflow counts and new problems.push rules without changing the stamp.

READ: `artifacts` state is never reset when sessionId changes, and a failed load keeps the old value (work-documents.tsx:83-98). The auditor's same-conversation path is weaker than stated. After adopt, run becomes null so enabled=false. When task B's first run frame arrives, a fetch fires and normally replaces A's list with B's (usually empty). A's file would then survive only if every B fetch failed. The same root cause has a more common trigger the auditor missed: ChatView is preserved across /chat/A to /chat/B (READ: chat-view.tsx:2233-2236 'App Router preserves this ChatView'). useConversationWork resets session, run and events on a conversation change (168-172) but not the artifact list. INFERRED: opening a chat whose task has already finished renders TerminalRun in the same batch that sets run (use-conversation-work.ts:206-207), before the list effect fetches. So the previous conversation's staged deliverable, with its title, Download link and rise-in animation, paints under the new task. Its inline preview also starts downloading, which can be a whole site zip. This happens on every switch between two task-bearing chats, and it persists if the fetch fails. That is why the severity is raised to medium.

READ: the inline preview passes active always true (work-site-preview.tsx:384,391,397). useSitePreview fetches the full zip via the download URL on every activation (445-457), and the download route sends Cache-Control 'private, no-store' (download/route.ts:147). The spreadsheet preview route buffers the whole object, hashes it and runs exceljs load (preview/route.ts:78-110; spreadsheet-preview.ts:129). There is no visibility or on-demand gating. It is mitigated because it mounts only for the newest task's terminal panel, and generated sites are usually small (typed blocks, with base64 assets capped per asset). So low is right, and the 40 MB scenario is an edge case.

READ: stagedArtifact returns null for non-previewable kinds (stage:33-43), and the slot uses empty:hidden (work-run-panel.tsx:356). The stage appears only in TerminalRun, and the 'under Outputs' line (stage:74-77) points to SessionOutputs, which builds tiles only from chat Artifacts (session-outputs.tsx:97-106) and contains no Work reference. Correction: .pdf is not a runner-generated kind (deliverables/index.ts:107-113), so the affected kinds are .docx and .pptx. Same root cause as defect 1.

READ: LiveRun renders WorkCurrentAction, Plan, WorkLiveMeter, RunWords and questions/approvals, with no documents (work-run-panel.tsx:212-307). WorkDeliverableStage is mounted only in TerminalRun (356-358). The stage's own comment, 'Rises in when the run first writes something worth staging' (stage:47-48), shows it was designed to appear mid-run on the old task page. The list is still fetched during the run (use-conversation-work.ts:244), just never drawn.

READ: the stage renders title, extension, version, age and one Download anchor (stage:46-79). It has no open-in-canvas, full-screen, version picker, copy, share, rename, delete, edit, ask-to-change or comment control. For sites, SitePreviewBody is a bare sandboxed iframe (work-site-preview.tsx:562-605). Navigation happens only through in-page links via the postMessage bridge. It has no page list, back or forward, or open-in-tab; 'Back to the first page' appears only on a page error (579-585). The dialog variant is also unmounted. For the merge goal this is the main feature gap.

Same evidence as defect 5. The stage never reads validatedAt (stage:41-80), and the schema comment at schema.prisma:2621-2623 promises the opposite. Combined with defect 3's false negatives, the verdict is also often wrong when it is recorded, but that argues for a fixed validator plus a shown verdict, not for hiding it.

Same evidence as defect 6. The limit:1 discovery is at use-conversation-work.ts:179-186, and one WorkRunPanel versus research history is at chat-view.tsx:2262-2266. It is aggravated by /work/<sessionId> links for older tasks resolving to the conversation, which then draws a different task (work/[[...segments]]/page.tsx:49-58).

missed.title: Archiving a task (e.g. from the Mac inbox) removes it and its deliverables from its web conversation
missed.evidence: READ: parseSessionListQuery defaults `archived: archived ?? false` (protocol.ts:935), and GET /api/work/sessions filters by it (sessions/route.ts:25-40). Conversation discovery calls fetchWorkSessions({conversationId, limit: 1}) without `archived` (use-conversation-work.ts:179; work-transport.tsx:455-458). adoptDiscoveredSession returns the discovered row or null (delegation.ts:99-106). Native can PATCH archived=true (NativeWorkClient.swift:505).
missed.failure_scenario: The user archives a finished task on the Mac to tidy the inbox. The next web discovery poll (4s) returns either nothing or an older non-archived task. The task panel, its staged report and its Download vanish from the chat that started it, with no way to reach them on web. Archiving acts as 'remove from the conversation', which is not what the user meant.

missed.title: /work/<sessionId> redirect ignores soft-deleted tasks despite its comment promising a 404
missed.evidence: READ: `prisma.workSession.findFirst({ where: { id: target.sessionId, userId: user.id } })` has no `deletedAt: null` (49-52). The comment at 53-56 says 'A task that was deleted … gets the 404'. WorkSession deletion is soft: `data: { deletedAt: new Date() }` (src/app/api/work/sessions/[id]/route.ts:107). Every other session read filters deletedAt (sessions/route.ts:31).
missed.failure_scenario: The user deletes a task and later clicks its link in a notification email. Instead of the promised 404, they are redirected into the conversation, which (because the list filters deleted rows) shows no task or a different one. The link reads as 'your work is here' and then shows nothing.
